window.why: 10 days in April 2026, the month Artemis II flew around the Moon. Earth rises from below the horizon (comm blackout) to above it, and the Sun sinks low at the outer sites.

sites.name: Shackleton Crater Rim
sites.notes: One of the sunniest spots on the Moon, on the rim of Shackleton crater (a 'Peak Near Shackleton' was an Artemis III candidate region in 2022). Ice is a short drive down into the crater.

sites.name: Shackleton Crater Floor

power_from.why: Game assumption: solar arrays up on the sunny rim, power sent down a long cable (half lost).

comm_from.why: Game assumption: the crater walls hide Earth, so radio goes through a relay on the rim.

sites.notes: Permanently shadowed: the Sun never reaches the floor, so it is colder than -170 C and can hold ice. Great for water, terrible for solar power.

sites.name: Connecting Ridge
sites.notes: The ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters; an Artemis III candidate region in 2022. Long sunlit stretches and views toward Earth.

sites.name: de Gerlache Crater Rim
sites.notes: Rim of de Gerlache crater ('de Gerlache Rim 2' is an Artemis III candidate region). Sunny rim next to a shadowed crater floor.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.notes: A 5 km-tall mountain (Mons Malapert) on the Earth-facing side of the pole, so Earth is above the horizon much more often: best for talking to Houston, farther from ice. Artemis III candidate region.
